property_summary: Only the current owner can change the owner state variable; the reference enforces this via the onlyOwner modifier, but the buggy version allows any caller to change owner.
For any address that is not the current owner, calling transferOwnership must not change the owner; the bug allows any caller to change owner, violating this rule.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must remain unchanged if the caller is not the current owner; the bug allows a non-owner to change the owner.
The owner is always the same after a transferOwnership call from the current owner, but the bug allows a non-owner to change it because the mutated onlyOwner modifier uses the negated condition.
For any non-owner caller, a call to transferOwnership should not change the owner state variable; the reference reverts, but the buggy version allows a non-owner to succeed and change the owner.
The reference contract ensures only the owner can change the owner, while the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner to any address.

After any sequence of calls made only by the owner, the owner address should remain equal to the last address passed to transferOwnership by the owner; the bug allows a non-owner to change the owner, violating this invariant.
After any call to `transferOwnership` made by anyone other than the current owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the bug allows such a call to change the owner.
If a caller is not the current owner, a transferOwnership call must always revert; the buggy modifier allows non-owner calls to succeed and change the owner.

After transferOwnership is called by the owner, the owner state variable should be set to the argument newOwner; the buggy version always sets it to msg.sender, so the two values differ whenever msg.sender and newOwner are different.
For any address a1 (initial owner) and a2 (newOwner) where a1 != a2, after a1 calls transferOwnership(a2), the owner must equal a2; the bug sets it to a1.
For any initial owner O and any new owner N, after O calls transferOwnership(N), the owner must become N; the buggy version sets owner to O instead.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner reverts if msg.sender is not the current owner; else the owner remains the current owner as long as the call is executed by the current owner and newOwner is not the same as msg.sender, the buggy version incorrectly sets owner to msg.sender instead of newOwner.
After the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must equal newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead.

The owned() function in the reference contract reverts for non-owner callers due to the onlyOwner modifier, while the buggy version succeeds for any caller; thus a call from a non-owner address reverts in the original but succeeds in the mutant.
Any call to owned() from an address that is not the owner must revert in the reference contract, but succeeds in the buggy version.
transferOwnership can only be called by the owner; the bug allows any non-owner to call it
After any non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner should remain unchanged; the bug lets a non-owner change the owner.
